neighbours.label: The second half of a 'the longer ..., the more ...' correlative, on its comma and 'the', in an explanatory passage; short standalone correlatives are weak.
fire: Habits form through repetition. The longer we repeat a routine, the more automatic it becomes in daily life.
Muscles adapt to load over time. Put simply, the heavier you are lifting, the stronger your arms become.
Rumours spread by being retold. The longer a story circulates, the more believable it becomes to listeners.
Fever follows the infection closely. In short, the sicker the patient is, the higher the temperature climbs.
Skills fade without practice. The longer we stay away from a language, the more distant it becomes in memory.
Prices react to scarcity. In other words, the rarer the metal is, the more valuable it becomes for traders.
Fear grows when it is fed. The longer we avoid a task, the more daunting it becomes in our minds.
Soil dries out in the heat. Put simply, the hotter the summer gets, the harder the ground becomes.
quiet: Habits form through repetition. We repeat a routine for weeks and it turns automatic in daily life.
Muscles adapt to load over time. Put simply, lifting heavy things will make your arms stronger.
Rumours spread by being retold. A story that circulates for years sounds believable to listeners.
Fever follows the infection closely. In short, a sick patient usually has a high temperature.
Skills fade without practice. We stayed away from the language and it grew distant in memory.
Prices react to scarcity. In other words, a rare metal is usually valuable for traders.
Fear grows when it is fed. We avoided the task for a month and it felt daunting.
Soil dries out in the heat. Put simply, a hot summer makes the ground hard.

predictions: 5-6/8 fire. Probes needed a lead-in sentence, so every item has one. 'In other words' alone reached 0.19.
notes: Probes: 0.72 and 0.41 with a lead-in, 0.05-0.23 without one, and 0.09-0.19 for lead-in passages with no correlative. The output promotes become/becoming, which fits a correlative's second clause. Top examples also include ' world', 'nummer' and ' off', so this covers part of the pole.
